title: Evaluating radiographic and clinical injury in myelopathic and non-myelopathic cervical spinal compression
text:
Cervical spinal cord compression may commonly present with subtle neurological complaints and is extremely
common in older individuals. However, little is known about the specific features that differentiate age-related
compression from clinical disease and how new myelopathic symptoms develop. This work seeks to develop
patient-specific imaging markers that define early disease development, improve our conceptual understanding
of how cord stress and injury progress contribute to disease and distinct clinical presentations, and characterize
subjects at early risk of subsequent myelopathic conversion.

title: A novel target in aged fracture healing
text:
Advanced age diminishes bone repair capacity and is associated with increased surgical intervention at the time
of the injury and subsequently due to the need for revisional surgery. Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) is a circulatory
protein which we show to increase in abundance with age and to have deleterious effects in bone fracture
healing. Here we propose to investigate the efficacy of using neutralizing antibodies temporally neutralize
circulating ApoE to improve aged fracture healing and to identify the mechanism by which ApoE is able to inhibit
bone repair and investigate the function of a newly identified osteoblastic cell-surface receptor, muscle-specific
kinase (MuSK).

title: MWCCS-DC: Surviving the HIV Epidemic using Cohort-driven Knowledge
text:
PUBLIC NARRATIVE
With treatment, people with HIV are living longer but develop brain and heart disease, as well as cancer, at
higher rates than the general population. Our research is focused on discovering the mechanism for this
increased risk and identify ways to improve health in persons aging with HIV. As our cohort also includes
persons without HIV, our findings will also provide insights into the mechanisms of these diseases among the
general population.

title: Promoting hearing aid use: The roles of social networks and daily interpersonal processes
text:
Although hearing loss is a leading source of disability among adults in the U.S., very few individuals with
hearing loss wear hearing aids at the recommended levels. Emerging evidence suggests that social ties and
support are key predictive factors in the adoption and use of hearing aids. The purpose of the proposed
longitudinal study is to understand links between social networks, daily interpersonal processes, and daily
hearing aid use among older adults who own hearing aids, which will lead to actionable recommendations for
interventions aimed at improving hearing aid use among older adults.

title: Regulation of Germ cell to maternal transition
text:
Germ cell differentiates into an oocyte that helps launch the next generation by supplying a maternal
contribution of RNAs, proteins, complexes, and organelles that is critical to establish a totipotent zygote.
Nevertheless, the mechanisms that establish this maternal contribution during oogenesis are incompletely
understood. Using Drosophila as a model system, my lab has discovered a germ cell-to-maternal transition,
wherein RNAs that promote germ cell-specific programs, such as those that promote germ cell differentiation,
and entry into meiosis are excluded from maternal contribution to promote fertility.

title: Pacific Island Partnership for Cancer Health for Everyone (PIPCHE)
text:
OVERALL
The Pacific Island Partnership for Cancer Health for Everyone (PIPCHE) represents the next step in augmenting a Hawai‘i-Guam-USAPI cancer research infrastructure by investing in Pacific Island Populations leaders, Early Stage Investigators, community partners, and community-research. As a result of the 22-year commitment, PIPCHE is also well positioned to increase the biomedical cancer science workforce and research leadership that better reflects the Hawai‘i-Guam-USAPI population and to stimulate new areas of cancer research. PIPCHE has assembled dedicated academic and community partnerships needed to synergistically accelerate cancer research into a sustainable forum that pursues cultural and environmental appropriate solutions.

title: CAGE-Enabled Single-Lineage RNA-Seq for Bacterial PERTURB-Seq and Host-Pathogen Interaction Analysis
text:
This research develops innovative technology to study bacterial genes and their functions with unprecedented
sensitivity, and how our immune system reacts to different pathogens. If successful, the tools piloted here
would help a large number of labs to investigate host-pathogen interactions and how genes control pathogen
function.

title: Molecular determinants of Streptococcus gordonii response to shear forces
text:
Fluid flow is common in multiple sites in the human body where bacteria can be found, contributing
to biofilm-associated diseases. The shear forces generated by fluid flow significantly affect biofilm
formation and maintenance; however, the cellular mechanisms utilized by bacteria to sense and
respond to these forces are broadly not understood. This proposal aims to broaden our molecular
understanding of the impact of fluid shear forces on bacterial cells in a biofilm so that we can
better treat biofilm-associated diseases.

title: Exploring Functional Divergence in Human and Chimpanzee Arteries: Implications for Cardiovascular Disease
text:
The factors that induce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, the leading cause of death
worldwide, are not fully understood despite decades of research. Study of our closest living
relative, the chimpanzee, could provide novel insights into the mechanism of this disease as they
rarely develop atherosclerotic lesions despite having higher serum cholesterol levels. I intend to
use two newly developed methods to create arterial endothelial cells from human, chimpanzee,
and human-chimpanzee hybrid cells to investigate species-specific changes in gene expression
that may underlie differences in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.

title: CLEAR Consortium: Discovering the Developmental Mechanisms of Trachea-Esophageal Birth Defects
text:
OVERALL | PROJECT NARRATIVE
The CLEAR Consortium is a unique multi-disciplinary team of clinicians, geneticists, computational scientists,
developmental and stem cell biologists using an innovative combination of patient genome sequencing, neonatal
MRI, animal models, single cell genomics, and human organoids. Our goal is to discover the developmental
mechanisms of life-threatening trachea-esophageal birth defects to better understand their etiology, enhance
diagnosis, improve treatment, and inform strategies to generate tissue in vitro for repair.

title: Targeting the Variable Region of the T-cell Receptor as a Therapeutic Strategy in Clonal T-cell Disease
text:
An effective paradigm for the optimized development of cancer therapeutics must entail an
integrated approach in which functional assay-based target identification is supported with
genomic and gene expression data. We hypothesize this functional genomics approach will
provide unparalleled mechanistic resolution to connect oncogenic TCR signaling cascades with
resistance to apoptosis. Our goal is to use this knowledge to identify promising treatment
strategies that positively impact patients with T cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.

title: A simple device for office evaluation of tubal patency during the workup for infertility.
text:
The gold standard procedure for evaluation of tubal patency in women suffering with infertility is the
hysterosalpingogram (HSG), a radiologic study that requires referral to a specialist and specialized equipment,
exposes women to ionizing radiation, and is often available only in urban areas, which means many women of
reproductive age do not have access to it. To streamline this initial diagnostic step in the infertility workup,
OryGyn Medical Devices, LLC is developing a medical device, the Tubal Selective Delivery System (TSDS),
which provides a simple and convenient office-based evaluation of obstructed fallopian tubes that does not
require imaging or referral to a specialist. Use of the TSDS would increase convenience for patients and
decrease cost of the initial steps of evaluating infertility.

title: Harnessing antibody-driven bioconjugation to modulate immune function
text:
Cell therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment, but their production remains a major barrier due to the
reliance on genetic engineering. This research plan outlines a chemical approach to manipulate immune cells
using proximity-driven bioconjugation, equipping them with the ability to target and eliminate cancer cells. These
reactions will also establish a platform to program synergistic immune responses by chemically modifying
cooperative immune receptors.

title: Core 2: Biorepository, Biomarker Analysis and GI Organoids
text:
CORE 2 NARRATIVE
Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is a potentially curative therapy for many malignant
diseases whose applicability has been impeded by the development of its most serious complication,
GI GVHD. Strategies that strengthen the target cells in the GI tract will allow for better harnessing of
this effective therapeutic modality. Core 2 provides support for organoid models, biomarker analysis
and computer programming, and is used by all three projects.

title: The Tisch Cancer Institute - Cancer Center Support Grant
text: The mission of the Tisch Cancer Institute is to accelerate the prevention and treatment of cancer, improving the lives of cancer patients and their families in our community. To accomplish this mission, the TCI has developed collaborative research programs that strive to translate discoveries into new therapies and to develop new prevention and delivery strategies with priority given to cancers affecting our catchment area.

title: Defining the Mechanistic Basis of Bacterial Androgen Production in Dampening Anti-Tumor Immunity and Promoting Resistance to Androgen Receptor Axis-Targeted Therapies for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
text:
Metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains a leading cause of cancer deaths in males and
there is a tremendous unmet clinical need to uncover mechanisms of therapeutic resistance in this patient
population. This study will discover and validate bacterial enzymatic pathways that are responsible for androgen
production in the gut that contributes to therapeutic resistance to immunotherapy and endocrine therapy in
mCRPC. We ultimately aim to identify a microbiome drug target for use in the development of targeted
therapeutics to overcome treatment resistance; as such, we anticipate that the knowledge gained from the
proposed studies could be translated to a therapeutic that could greatly impact the lives of individuals with
advanced mCRPC.

title: Investigation of the rules dictating plasma cell longevity
text: Mucosal interfaces generate most of the plasma cells in the body, which may achieve a long-lived state in the bone marrow and the gut lamina propria. Understanding their maturation process towards longevity will ultimately impact rational vaccine design against infectious diseases.

title: Exploiting Alzheimer's disease patient-derived stem cells to biochemically define tau and amyloid-beta oligomer toxic features and their downstream cellular effects
text:
The proposed research is relevant to the public health because more than 6 million Americans are currently
living with Alzheimer's disease and desperately need life-improving therapeutics. Upon conclusion, we will
provide the Alzheimer's research community with a new source of disease-causing Ab and tau oligomers and
direct new targeting therapies by defining the structural components of a toxic oligomer. Additionally, we will
build a tool to describe complex intercellular network responses to Ab and tau oligomers opening yet another
line of therapeutic discovery.

title: Vitamin A metabolism at the host-microbiome interface
text:
Aberrations in epithelial barrier repair underlie multiple diseases, from IBD to CRC. Both microbes and dietary
nutrients are implicated in disease pathogenesis; however, precise underlying mechanisms remain unknown.
The proposed work will provide molecular and cellular insights into how gut bacteria promote tissue regeneration
by regulating cellular vitamin A metabolism and T-cell responses.

title: Single-molecule protein sequencing: resolving individual amino acids via commercially accessible nanopores
text:
The ability to interrogate amino acid sequences and their modifications at the ultimate level of individual
molecules and without prior knowledge has the potential to enhance fundamental understanding of complex
biological processes at a cellular level. Glyphic Biotechnologies proposes to commercialize a novel method of
single-molecule protein sequencing (SMPS) based on spatial distancing of amino acids through the generation
of a biopolymer that preserves their native sequence and post-translational modifications and allows them to be
read through commercially available nanopores. As the first application out of many possible, this method will be
applied to sequencing neoantigens, showcasing the use of Glyphic SMPS in enabling a precision approach to
personalized treatments.
